reason: Refuted as specified under the feasibility/schedule lens. The pieces are feasible, but the gate's thresholds and its prescribed action fail. (1) The tool part is easy and safe. The lines '[ds] detection+edges X s' and '[ds] repair X s' (plus run_stats repair_seconds) are in every dummy log, and dummy_gates.py has no timing gate yet. It is ~0.5 h of offline code, with no kernel change, LB slot or R8 issue. (2) The GPU threshold sits inside same-code noise. Across 6 dummies with IDENTICAL GPU code (exp56, 57b, K2=58, K1=58t, FD, FF), per-clip detection+edges ranged 211-233, 210-246, 205-230 and 230-268 s. exp56 vs K2 is +19/+32/+18/+32 s (mean +25). So '> 15 s/clip-shard vs the K2 dummy' false-FAILs on pure host jitter. The only planned rider that touches the GPU is K4 tempfuse (S6), which lands exactly in this noise. The fallback 'median of 2 dummies' then becomes the normal case, at ~0.5 GPU-h per extra dummy from the ~11 h quota shared with the exp60 lab. (3) The tail gate is usable only as a MEAN over clips (sum over 4 clips > 32 s). Same-code repair noise is -1.0..+6.4 s/clip (K1 vs 57b), and K2 itself is +11.3 s on 6bba_05db0fb1 vs 57b, so a per-clip reading fails K2. (4) The prescribed action is the harmful part. The rule 'rebuild with DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=32400, REPAIR stays 34200' is byte-identical when off and needs no builder change. But it is not fail-soft in value. Step-0 model sim (repair 61 s + insertion 66 s/clip, degraded 28.2 s, 1e-5 per inserted clip, 1e-4 per fully repaired clip): at s = 1.0-1.2 it gains +1e-4..+2.7e-4. At s >= 1.2-1.3 (N 97-106), and at every s for N = 130, it loses 0.0006-0.0022, because the 0.5 h gap lets insertion eat the repair budget and pushes later clips into degraded repair. Under a guessed slowdown prior (the anchor is an upper bound) its EV is -2e-5..-5e-5. For comparison, 8.5/9.5 gives about +1e-5..+3e-5, and 9.0 with REPAIR 37800 gives +8e-5..+3e-4 but needs the H1 rule rewrite and a user OK. The hidden run stays under 12 h (Tmax 10.1-10.4 h), so this is not a timeout risk, but it contradicts FINAL_REPORT v3 l.57 and the l2 value verdict ('never move DIVINS alone'). (5) The attribution benefit is already available for free: a rider's own latency <= 8.0 h proves the insertion gate never fired. (6) Part (b), recording that FD's local 0.9249 > 0.9180 is the in-sample 'trust ILP over relink' trap, is a zero-cost CONTEXT note. It is not there yet, and it is feasible now.
fix: Adopt in reduced form. (a) Add a report-only runtime ledger to dummy_gates.py that prints WARN, never FAIL. The tail check is the mean over clips of Δrepair_seconds vs the K2 dummy, warning at > 8 s/clip (sum > 32 s over the 4 dummy clips). Run the GPU check only when the rider patches the GPU phase (K4 tempfuse). There, compare each clip's detection+edges with the median of the 6 existing same-code dummies (211.5/215.0/211.0/234.7 s), warning at > +10% (a guess; same-code spread is up to +15%). A forecast line reports T = L(K2) observed (or 7.86 h) + N*Δtail + (N/2)*ΔGPU, with N = 106. (b) A WARN does NOT trigger a DIVINS-only rebuild. Keep 28800/34200. Accept the rider, and judge it only if its observed latency is <= 8.0 h. If it is > 8.0 h, note the confound under R4. If the forecast is > 8.5 h, either drop the rider or, with the user's explicit OK for the H1 rule rewrite, move BOTH deadlines together (32400/37800, keeping a gap >= 1.5 h). (c) Check that DIVINS_DEADLINE_S is in the built notebook's probe.json and SAFETAIL line statically. Run no extra dummy. (d) Record part (b) in CONTEXT now: FD 0.9249 (44b6_0113de3b 0.868 -> 0.961) is an in-sample artefact, like edge filter #29/#30, and must not be acted on.
realistic_gain: ~0 on score. The ledger prevents a mis-attributed rider in rare slow worlds (EV ~1e-5) and costs 0.5 agent-h, 0 slots and 0 GPU if run report-only. As written, the rebuild rule has EV of about -2e-5..-5e-5, with a -0.001..-0.002 tail at s >= 1.2-1.3 or N >= 130. Part (b) is worth 0 on score but protects against a false lead.
